title: vLLM-HUST Ascend official runtime support matrix

scope.policy: Only public, upstream release images are deployable. Nightly, main, model-specialized, mirror-only, and credential-gated artifacts are discovery-only and are not approved baselines.

stack.commit_provenance: The commits are the public v0.23.0 tag targets. The OCI image config has no source-revision label or signed provenance tying image bytes to those commits, so this association is official-release-reference, not a cryptographic build attestation.

repository_identity.policy: vllm-hust and vllm-ascend-hust were rebuilt directly from their official upstream repositories. Current validation must use commits reachable from the rebuilt upstream-rooted history; pre-rebuild commits and old fork-only history must not be treated as current source identity.
repository_identity.evidence_rule: A repository rebuild is a source-identity boundary. Earlier NPU evidence remains a historical receipt but cannot verify the rebuilt repositories until the workload is rerun with new reachable commits. Branch names are never evidence identities; record all 40 hexadecimal commit IDs.

source_profiles.compatibility: This is the only stable released source/image pair in this manifest. It does not verify either rebuilt HUST main branch.

No immutable stable image is published for this exact commit pair. Build with VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty, rebuild plugin/native extensions, and run real-NPU acceptance before promotion. The core build-isolation torch pin alone is not proof of a runtime conflict.
The plugin main Dockerfiles default VLLM_TAG to v0.27.1, but vLLM Ascend has no v0.27.1 stable release. Treat this as an upstream development/CI candidate, not an official stable runtime.

access_policy.image: Anonymous public pull from Quay.io; no credentials are stored. Regional mirrors are not authoritative and are excluded from digest pinning.
access_policy.driver_firmware: Select the exact product on the Huawei Ascend download portal. Download may require accepting the Huawei EULA and, depending on region/package, signing in or administrator/vendor entitlement.
access_policy.secrets: Do not place registry tokens, Huawei IDs, cookies, SSH keys, or download URLs containing signed query parameters in this manifest or its evidence.

known_gaps.item: No official Windows, macOS, ppc64le, or riscv64 vLLM-Ascend runtime image
known_gaps.impact: Only linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 appear in the v0.23.0 OCI indexes

known_gaps.item: Ascend 910/910 Pro B and Atlas 200I A2 (310B)
known_gaps.impact: Upstream FAQ marks these families unsupported/unplanned
Official 310P image explicitly uninstalls Triton and Triton Ascend
Release images expose no source-revision label or verifiable build attestation; tag commits are reference commits only
Huawei publishes product-specific HDK compatibility tables; administrators must select the exact server/card product

known_gaps.item: All eight current variants after the upstream repository rebuild
known_gaps.impact: The A2/openEuler receipt predates the rebuild; no current rebuilt-source commit pair has real-NPU evidence
No stable official image identifies the exact ed9f108/660da85 commit pair; stable v0.23.0 images and mutable nightly snapshots must not be presented as matching it
At the recorded snapshot the tag is a single linux/amd64 manifest and has no linux/arm64 image

known_conflicts.details: Some historical documentation still names v0.17.0rc1/CANN 8.5.1 while the active runtime helper and this matrix use v0.23.0/CANN 9.1.0. The current/default wording must follow this matrix; old versions are rollback-only.
An upstream report shows v0.23.0/310P initialization failure on driver 25.5.2 while v0.22.1rc1 worked; use the documented 26.0.RC1 line pending upstream closure.
A tag can be repointed. Production and evidence runs must pull the index digest and record the selected ARM64 manifest digest.

The rebuilt core/plugin main branches move independently. The plugin main Dockerfiles target vLLM v0.27.1, current stable images target v0.23.0, and the captured HUST core main is newer than both. None of these identities is interchangeable.

known_conflicts.item: Core build isolation versus Ascend runtime Torch
known_conflicts.details: The captured core pyproject build system requests Torch 2.13.0 while the plugin runtime pins Torch 2.10.0. Ascend builds use VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty, so this observation is a build/runtime split requiring overlay-build tests, not by itself proof of a runtime dependency conflict.

Ubuntu nightly manifests observed vLLM v0.27.1 while openEuler ARM64 configs were older v0.26.0 builds; the Ubuntu A5 nightly was amd64-only. Nightly tags are mutable and fail closed as discovery-only.

administrator_actions: Identify each host's exact Atlas product/SKU before downloading HDK packages.
Obtain the matching driver and firmware from Huawei's official portal, accept applicable EULA, and store packages in an organization-controlled restricted artifact store.
Record package filename, vendor-published checksum when present, locally computed SHA-256, acquisition date, and access ticket outside this public repository; never record credentials or signed URLs.
Capture firmware output in the next 910B2 acceptance run; the existing 2026-08-19 evidence records driver but omits firmware.
Schedule real-NPU acceptance for all eight stable variants against commits reachable from the rebuilt upstream-rooted repositories.
Decide whether the organization wants a release-pinned v0.23.0 validation lane or a separately built current-main lane; do not overlay current main into the v0.23.0 image and reuse the old status.
